// why: TWO JOBS, AND THEY MOVED APART AT 1.0.0. This file CHECKS; tsconfig.build.json
EMITS. Until 1.0.0 there was no second file and no emit at all, because
`exports` pointed straight at ./src/*.js and a build step would have changed
the artifact every consumer receives. That is no longer true: the source is
TypeScript, so the artifact HAS to be compiled, and `exports` now names
./dist/*.js. The policy did not fail — its premise did.
`checkJs` stays on with nothing left to check: the include list named four
.js files one at a time, they were the last JavaScript under src/, and they
converted. The flag is kept rather than deleted because tsconfig.build.json
extends this file and turns it OFF there — that pair is what let the tree
move a layer at a time — and because a .js file added tomorrow should be
checked by default now, which is the opposite of the rule this replaced.
`verbatimModuleSyntax` is not a style preference. A type-only import inside
a .vue `lang="ts"` block is erased by tsc but SURVIVES the consumer's
per-file esbuild transform, and lands as a runtime `does not provide an
export named`. Requiring `import type` makes that unshippable.
`erasableSyntaxOnly` bans enum, namespace and parameter properties — every
construct that compiles to something other than itself. It is what lets a
conversion commit be reviewed as a diff of dist/: the emitted file must be
the source minus its annotations, and nothing else.
`types/` is HAND-WRITTEN and is the package's documented public surface. It
is not generated and it is not the emitter's output. It is included so that
a syntax error or a broken import in one fails `npm run typecheck` here
rather than in a consumer's editor.
`typings/` is repository-internal ambient declarations — *.vue, *.css and
the untyped globals — and is deliberately NOT in package.json#files: a
`declare module '*.vue'` shipped to a consumer would override their own.
